title: Solomon Dedicates the Temple
summary: Solomon brings the ark into the Temple at Jerusalem, the glory of the LORD fills the house, and he prays the prayer of dedication (1 Kgs 8; 2 Chr 5–7).
description: DATE CONFLICT: CFAH-1 Table 1 lists 1012 BC as "Solomon Dedicates the Temple", but Jones's Chart No. 1 has 1012 BC as the year Solomon BEGINS the Temple (2992 AM), and Ussher dates the foundation to 1012 BC (§465) and the dedication to 1004 BC (3001 AM, §468), after 7½ years of building (1 Kgs 6:37–38). Per the owner's sort rule this record sorts on the Table 1 value (1012 BC) pending clarification. Jordan (secondary, display only) separates the two: foundation AM 2993 (937 B.C. SBC), completion AM 3000, dedication AM 3014.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones baseline): 1012 BC (Solomon Dedicates the Temple) (no higher-tier year available).

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
chronologies.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point. CONFLICT: Jones Chart No. 1 (CFAH's stated baseline) gives 1012 BC for the BEGINNING of the Temple; Ussher has foundation 1012 BC and dedication 1004 BC. Table 1's "Dedicates" may be a labelling error.

chronologies.citation: Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament: A Return to the Basics, 23rd ed. (Master Books, 2026), Appendix F, printed p. 279 (PDF p. 314)
chronologies.note: The 23rd ed. prints the dedication in 1004 BC. Chart No. 1 dated the beginning, not the dedication; that older note is replaced by this printed dedication. The founding in 1012 BC is on founding-of-solomons-temple. CFAH-1 Table 1 keeps the sort at 1012 BC.

chronologies.date: Building begun in the 480th year after the Exodus, 4th year of Solomon, month Zif; finished in the 11th year, month Bul (7 years); dedicated at the feast in the 7th month Ethanim

chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fifth Age §465–468 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
chronologies.note: §465 (2992c AM, 1012 BC): foundation laid "on the second day of the second month (called Zif, Monday May 21st)"; §467 (3000a AM, 1005 BC): finished, dedication postponed because a Jubilee year; §468 (3001a AM, 1004 BC): dedication in the 7th month.

chronologies.date: Dedicated in the 7th month, "the first month of the next year, the year 3014" (after Temple and palace were completed in 3013)
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Jubilee, Part 2," Biblical Chronology 5:3 (March 1993), section "The Building of the Temple"
chronologies.note: Jordan: "The Temple was dedicated ... in the seventh month, but of which year we are not told ... We are virtually forced to assume ... the year 3014." DIFFERS from CFAH-1 Table 1 (1012 BC "dedicates") and Ussher (dedication 3001 AM / 1004 BC).

chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), chart "Anno Mundi / B.C. (SBC) / B.C. (CCC)" at the start of the article
chronologies.note: FOUNDATION, not dedication: "In this year, A.M. 2993, the foundations of the Temple were laid. The Temple was completed seven years later, A.M. 3000" (BC 4:8 §4; BC 2:8 "The Temple Connection"). One year later than Jones/Ussher (2992 AM). In 1990 (BC 2:8) Jordan gave "932 B.C." following Anstey and Mauro; the SBC chart (1993) gives 937. CCC on same chart: 966 B.C. B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years. Restated in From Creation to Solomon (No. 2, 2001), ch. 11, p. 53: "2993 - Foundation of Temple laid, 480 years after Exodus." and "3000 - Completion of Temple."

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 11, chart table "Biblical History According To A.M & B.C. Dates"
chronologies.note: This is the year the temple was COMPLETED (page 10 also has "2993 AM Temple work began"). The dedication (this record) is not dated separately; Jordan himself assumes the dedication in AM 3014 (BC "Jubilee, Part 2"). Differs from Jordan's own published figure(s): AM 3014, 2993. The compilation's B.C. year (1010) is AM subtracted from 4010 (its own convention: Creation 4010 B.C.); Jordan's own SBC B.C. figures differ (here 937 B.C.). Display only; never converted or used for sorting.

chronologies.date: Building begun in Solomon's 4th year, 2nd month: "five hundred and ninety-two years after the Exodus", 1,020 years after Abraham came into Canaan, 1,440 after the deluge, 3,102 from Adam
chronologies.note: Josephus dates the START of building, not the dedication, and his intervals differ from 1 Kgs 6:1 (480th year).

chronologies.date: "from the Departing out of Egypt untill the building of the temple of Sollomon" 480 years
chronologies.citation: Annals of Clonmacnoise (trans. Mageoghagan 1627, ed. Murphy 1896), prefatory "Memorandum" table of the ages of the world (between the p. 8 and p. 11 running heads; OCR)
chronologies.note: Interval to the BUILDING of the Temple, not the dedication. The Memorandum lists intervals 1656, 0292, 0500, 0480, 0410, 0432, 0134 against seven rows; the row/number pairing is read from OCR column order and should be checked against the page scan.

chronologies.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 99; Julius Africanus, in the editor's biographical notice (the notice says it is abridged from Bunsen)
chronologies.note: Editor's summary in the biographical notice, which says it is abridged from Bunsen. Not a verbatim fragment. The year of the world is left in the quotation. It is not stored and it is not converted. The table prints A.M. 4457. The record this is placed on is the dedication of the Temple. The table says the building.

chronologies.date: “744 years assigned by him as the period between the Exodus and the building of the Temple”
chronologies.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 99; Julius Africanus, in the editor's biographical notice (the notice says it is abridged from Bunsen)
chronologies.note: Editor's summary in the biographical notice, which says it is abridged from Bunsen. Not a verbatim fragment. The year of the world is left in the quotation. It is not stored and it is not converted. Our check (not a figure of the text): the table's 4457 minus 3705 is 752, not 744.

chronologies.citation: Hales, A New Analysis of Chronology and Geography, History and Prophecy, 2nd ed., corrected and improved (London: C. J. G. & F. Rivington, 1830), vol. II, Synopsis of the Chronology, p. xxxv
chronologies.note: He prints “finished”. The record is the dedication.

open_questions: Does CFAH intend 1012 BC as the Temple foundation (as Jones's Chart No. 1 and Ussher) or dedication (as printed in CFAH-1 Table 1)? The 23rd ed. (2026) Appendix F prints the dedication at 1004 BC. Ask the authors. The 2019 PDF was not used.
